name: Slack
oneLiner: Creating a Slack OAuth app and distributing it unlisted takes under an hour with no review, but since May 2025 unlisted commercial apps get 1 req/min on conversations.history/replies and the Marketplace (10+ active workspaces, up to ~12 weeks of review) is the only sanctioned commercial channel.

verdict.activeEffort: 30–60 min for an unlisted distributed app; 1–3 days of prep for a Marketplace submission
verdict.approvalWait: None for unlisted distribution; Marketplace: preliminary review up to 10 business days + functional review up to 10 weeks (Slack's stated maxima)
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: Same day — install to your own workspace right after creating the app
verdict.timeToProduction: Same day for unlisted public distribution (with degraded history rate limits); roughly 2–12+ weeks for a Marketplace listing, after first reaching 10 active workspaces
verdict.reviewTrigger: Only a Slack Marketplace listing is reviewed; unlisted distribution is not. But commercially distributed unlisted apps get Tier 1 limits on conversations.history/replies (new apps and new installs since 2025-05-29; existing installs scheduled from 2026-03-03), and the API Terms name the Marketplace as the only appropriate commercial channel.

fastPath: Start today with Composio's managed Slack OAuth app — Composio lists Slack (SLACK) under 'Composio-managed OAuth available', so users can connect before your own app exists (confirm the OAuth scheme via the toolkit's composio_managed_auth_schemes field). In parallel, create your own app from a manifest, install it to your own workspace for testing, and activate public distribution for pilot customers while you accumulate the 10 active workspaces needed to apply for the Marketplace.

steps.title: Create the app from a manifest
steps.detail: Go to https://api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → 'From a manifest' → choose a development workspace → paste a YAML/JSON manifest (display_information.name, features.bot_user, oauth_config.redirect_urls, oauth_config.scopes.bot / .user, settings.token_rotation_enabled) → Next → review summary → Create. Alternatively an agent can call apps.manifest.create with an app configuration token.

steps.title: Generate an app configuration token (only if automating via API)
steps.detail: On api.slack.com/apps, scroll below your app list to 'Your App Configuration Tokens' → Generate Token for a workspace. The token expires after 12 hours; rotate with tooling.tokens.rotate using the refresh_token. A human must do this while logged into Slack; the agent can then drive apps.manifest.create / apps.manifest.update.

steps.title: Choose bot vs user token scopes
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions → Scopes. 'Bot Token Scopes' produce an xoxb- token acting as the app's bot user (preferred: e.g. chat:write, channels:read, channels:history, users:read). 'User Token Scopes' produce an xoxp- token acting as the authorizing user (needed for things like search:read). Request the minimum — admins see and judge the scope list at install time.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs and copy credentials
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs → Add New Redirect URL (HTTPS, e.g. your callback such as https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add if using Composio custom auth) → Save URLs. Basic Information → App Credentials: copy Client ID, Client Secret, Signing Secret.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation and PKCE before shipping
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions → enable Token Rotation (or manifest settings.token_rotation_enabled: true) if you want 12-hour access tokens (xoxe.) plus single-use refresh tokens (xoxe-1-). It cannot be turned off once enabled. PKCE (GA since 2026-03-30) is also enabled in OAuth & Permissions and marks the app a public client; reversing requires Slack support. Server-side agents usually need neither PKCE nor rotation, but rotation is good hygiene if your token store handles refresh.

steps.title: Run the OAuth flow against your own workspace
steps.detail: Send a user to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=...&scope=<bot scopes>&user_scope=<user scopes>&redirect_uri=...&state=... then exchange the code at POST https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access. Response has access_token (bot, xoxb-) and authed_user.access_token (user, xoxp-) when user scopes were requested.

steps.title: Complete the distribution checklist
steps.detail: Settings → Manage Distribution → 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces' → complete every checklist item (OAuth redirect URLs added, all URLs — redirect, interactivity, slash command, options load, Events API — on HTTPS, and confirm removal of hard-coded info such as tokens/workspace IDs) → tick the acknowledgment → Activate Public Distribution. You then get a shareable install URL / Add to Slack button.

steps.title: Make the app org-ready if you target Enterprise Grid customers
steps.detail: Add at least one bot scope, then sidebar → Org Level Apps → Opt-In → 'Yes, Opt-in' (manifest settings.org_deploy_enabled: true). An Org Admin must approve/install org-wide and then pick workspaces (direct them to https://app.slack.com/manage/ENTERPRISE_ID/integrations/profile/APP_ID/workspaces/add). Handle is_enterprise_install: true (team is null) in oauth.v2.access responses.

steps.title: Check the 2025 rate-limit and data-use terms against your agent's design
steps.detail: Unlisted commercially distributed apps created on/after 2025-05-29 (and new installs of older ones; existing installs were scheduled to follow on 2026-03-03) are limited to 1 request/minute on conversations.history and conversations.replies with limit max/default 15. Internal custom apps and Marketplace apps keep 50+/min and 1,000 objects. The developer policy also prohibits using Slack API data to train LLMs. If your agent reads channel history, plan for Marketplace listing.

phases.title: Slack Marketplace submission (optional, recommended for commercial apps)
phases.duration: Up to ~12 weeks (waiting on Slack), after reaching 10 active workspaces

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Submission is blocked until the app is installed on 10+ workspaces active in the last 28 days. Use unlisted distribution with pilot customers to get there.

steps.title: Prepare and submit the listing
steps.detail: Settings → Manage Distribution → Submit to Slack Marketplace. Provide listing copy, scope-by-scope justifications, a reviewer install path, test credentials with dummy data for any third-party service, and (recommended) a demo video of install → OAuth → use → uninstall. Remove disallowed scopes (identity.*, search:read, admin.*, legacy read/post/client, triggers:*). Run the automated checks first.

steps.title: Wait for preliminary and functional review, then publish
steps.detail: Preliminary review: feedback within up to 10 business days (resubmitting during this stage resets queue position). Functional review: up to 10 weeks for new apps, 6 weeks for updates. After approval you publish from app settings. Review cannot be expedited for launch dates.

requirements.item: Slack workspace you can install apps into
requirements.detail: Needed to create the app (a 'development workspace') and to test. Workspaces may restrict installs to admins or require approval, so use one where you are an admin.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL and HTTPS request URLs
requirements.detail: All OAuth redirect URLs and Events/interactivity/options URLs must use SSL before public distribution can be activated.
Distribution checklist asks you to confirm you have removed hard-coded information; tokens must come from per-workspace OAuth.

requirements.item: Secure token storage (and refresh handling if rotation enabled)
requirements.detail: Store per-workspace bot/user tokens; with rotation, store every new single-use refresh token (xoxe-1-) returned by oauth.v2.access.
Installed on at least 10 workspaces active in the past 28 days before you can submit to the Marketplace.

requirements.item: Reviewer test access and demo video (Marketplace only)
requirements.detail: Reviewers cannot use your Slack workspaces; provide an install path, dummy-data test accounts for your service, and ideally a video of the full OAuth + uninstall flow.

requirements.item: Compliance with API Terms / developer policy
requirements.detail: No bulk export or LLM training on Slack API data; Marketplace is the stated channel for commercial distribution.

scopes.purpose: Bot posts messages in channels it is a member of
Read public channel messages (conversations.history/replies) — subject to Tier 1 (1 req/min, 15 objects) for non-Marketplace commercial apps since 2025-05-29
Read direct messages the app is part of; same history rate-limit regime
Look up workspace members (add users:read.email for emails)
User-token scope to search messages/files; listed as not allowed for Marketplace apps
Admin API scopes for Enterprise org administration; not allowed for Marketplace listing and require an org admin to install

technical.pkce: supported (opt-in in OAuth & Permissions, GA 2026-03-30; required for custom URI scheme redirects; one-way switch to public client)
technical.refreshTokens: By default bot/user tokens never expire and no refresh token is issued. With token rotation enabled (irreversible), access tokens expire after 12 h (expires_in 43200, xoxe. prefix) and single-use refresh tokens (xoxe-1-) are redeemed at oauth.v2.access with grant_type=refresh_token.
technical.redirectUriRules: redirect_uri must match a URL registered under OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs; HTTPS required for public distribution; custom URI schemes require PKCE.
gotchas: Bot scopes go in the 'scope' param and user scopes in 'user_scope'; the user token comes back nested under authed_user.access_token.

Non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps: conversations.history/replies limited to 1 req/min, 15 messages per call — immediately for apps created and installs made from 2025-05-29, and (per Slack's changelog) for existing installs from 2026-03-03. Fatal for agents that read channel context.
Token rotation and PKCE are both one-way switches.
Apps with scopes beyond bot/incoming-webhook/commands/identify are uninstalled automatically when the installing user leaves the workspace or becomes a guest.
Enterprise Grid org installs return team: null and is_enterprise_install: true; many methods then need team_id.
Deactivating public distribution uninstalls the app from every workspace except the original.

blockers.blocker: History rate limit for unlisted commercial apps
blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 / ratelimited errors from conversations.history after one call per minute; responses capped at 15 messages
blockers.resolution: Get listed in the Slack Marketplace (requires 10 active workspaces + review), or if the use is internal to one company, ship as an internal custom app.

blockers.symptom: Activate Public Distribution button stays disabled in Manage Distribution
blockers.resolution: Switch every URL to HTTPS, add redirect URLs, remove hard-coded tokens, then tick the checklist.

blockers.blocker: Customer workspace requires admin approval or Marketplace-only apps
blockers.symptom: User sees a 'request to install' flow instead of Allow; or the install is blocked by the workspace's app management settings
blockers.resolution: Have the customer's admin approve the request; for Grid, opt in to Org Level Apps and have an Org Admin install org-wide; long term, list in the Marketplace.

blockers.blocker: Marketplace submission blocked by install count or disallowed scopes
blockers.symptom: Cannot submit (fewer than 10 active workspaces) or preliminary review returns feedback on scopes such as search:read or admin.*
blockers.resolution: Grow pilot installs via unlisted distribution; drop disallowed scopes and justify every remaining one.

blockers.blocker: Lost refresh token after enabling rotation
blockers.resolution: Persist the new refresh_token from every refresh response atomically; refresh before the 12 h expiry.

agentCan: Write the app manifest (scopes, redirect URLs, token rotation, org_deploy_enabled) and create/update the app via apps.manifest.create/update once given a configuration token
Implement the authorize redirect, oauth.v2.access code exchange, refresh handling and Enterprise-install branching
Fill the distribution checklist fields and draft Marketplace listing copy and scope justifications
Run the automated Marketplace pre-checks and record a scripted demo flow
humanMust: Log in to Slack and own/admin the development workspace; generate the app configuration token
Decide irreversible settings (token rotation, PKCE) and accept the API Terms / developer policy
Get 10 real customer workspaces actively using the app and sign off the Marketplace submission
Work with customer workspace / Org Admins to approve installs

uncertainties: Slack documents maximum review times (10 business days + up to 10 weeks) but real-world turnaround varies with queue volume; the actual estimate is only shown on the submission page.
The exact wording of the Manage Distribution checklist (e.g. 'Remove Hard Coded Information') was not visible in public docs we fetched — it is shown in the dashboard; marked reported.
Whether redirect_uri may be a sub-path of a registered URL (historically allowed) was not re-verified for oauth/v2.
Whether the 'commercially distributed' Tier 1 history limit is enforced for non-commercial/free unlisted apps is not spelled out; the changelog speaks of all unlisted apps outside the Marketplace.
Whether Composio's managed Slack app is itself Marketplace-listed (and so exempt from the history rate limit) was not verified.
The developer policy's LLM-training prohibition effective date and exact text were taken from search snippets plus news coverage, not a full read of the policy.

Whether Slack actually enforced the March 3, 2026 date for existing installs (or postponed it) could not be confirmed from a post-March 2026 official notice; the current conversations.history reference page still lists only 'Tier 3: 50+ per minute'.

verificationNotes: curl POST https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access with fake client_id/secret and code returned {"ok":false,"error":"invalid_code"} — Slack reports the code error before validating the client, so this endpoint cannot be used to sanity-check credentials.
curl POST oauth.v2.access with grant_type=refresh_token and a fake xoxe-1- token returned {"ok":false,"error":"invalid_refresh_token"}.
GET https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with a fake client_id returns HTTP 200 and a JS-rendered shell; the client_id error text is not visible without a browser, so not tested.
Corrected assumption: PKCE is no longer early-access-only — it went GA on 2026-03-30 and is self-serve, but irreversible.

Verified the May 2025 change: Tier 1 (1 req/min, limit max/default 15) on conversations.history and conversations.replies for unlisted apps created on/after 2025-05-29 and for new installs of older unlisted apps; internal custom apps and Marketplace apps unaffected. (Existing installs: see verifier correction below.)
Did not create a Slack app (no credentials used).

Verifier corrected: the guide said existing installs of unlisted apps are unaffected by the history rate limit. Slack's developer changelog (api.slack.com/changelog) states the new limits 'will be applied to existing installations' of unlisted distributed apps on March 3, 2026, so as of Oct 2026 all installs of non-Marketplace commercial apps should be assumed limited.

Verifier confirmed against docs.slack.dev (Marketplace review guide, token rotation, PKCE changelog): 10+ workspaces active in past 28 days; preliminary review up to 10 business days, functional up to 10 weeks; rotated tokens expire in 43,200 s and rotation can't be turned off; PKCE GA 2026-03-30, one-way, makes the app a public client.
